Hi Alex / Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team seemed enthusiastic about the latency profile and the Dedicated throughput options. Attached is an updated MAP (v3) that captures the evaluation milestones we discussed and the acceptance gates.

Quick note on timing: you mentioned procurement would need a formal SOW + vendor risk questionnaire signed off by your InfoSec team. Do you have an ETA on the procurement window? That will directly affect the go-live timeline and the MAP acceptance dates.

To keep things actionable I put together a short risk log and two re-baseline proposals (A = conservative, B = accelerated with parallel tasks). Please review the attached and let me know which approach you'd prefer. If procurement is the blocker, we can scope a staged deployment (pilot shard + reduced seat count) to meet the original business milestone while procurement completes the full POC.

Attachments: [Attachment: Novacare_MAP_v3.pdf (pdf, 420KB)], [Attachment: Procurement_Risk_Log_20260521.xlsx (xlsx, 110KB)]

- You: confirm procurement ETA / required documents by EOD Mon (5/24)
- Us (Jordan): scope pilot config and estimated costs for staged deployment by Tue (5/25)
- Us (Markus): draft conditional terms for pilot (short-term SLA & data compartmentalization) by Wed (5/26)

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if that speeds approvals.

Thanks,

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the map and the clear options. Short answer: procurement timeline is the issue. Our procurement and InfoSec are aligned but the internal vendor review committee meets every other Wednesday; the next meeting is 2-Jun. That effectively pushes the formal sign-off ~2–3 weeks beyond the dates in your MAP v3.

We can try to compress by circulating a clean SOW today, but InfoSec is insisting on a short vendor questionnaire + SOC 2 evidence. I'll attach the list they need. If you can provide the SOC evidence page and the redacted data flow diagram, that will help.

Maya and I like the staged pilot idea. If Redwood can run a pilot in our dev environment with masked data and a short-term SLA, we could validate integration and hit the internal stakeholder milestone on the original date, while procurement finishes the contract.

I propose: pilot start 5/29, pilot end 6/11, final sign-off 6/18 (if procurement stays on track). That shifts final go-live about 2 weeks.

Alex
Director, Platform Integrations
Novacare Health

Chloe / Jordan — quick read: pilot-only agreements are doable but we should avoid contractual exposure beyond operational metadata. Proposed approach:

- Short "Pilot SOW Addendum" (1 page) that attaches to a Master Services Agreement template but is explicitly time-boxed (max 3 weeks) and cancellable with 7 days' notice. No long-term indemnities; Redwood will provide SOC 2 summary and redacted DFD.
- Include a pilot uptime objective (not a full SLA) and a credit formula capped at a small percentage of pilot fees in case of significant outage (this keeps procurement comfortable without long-term SLA commitment).
- If Novacare requires additional controls, we can propose an interim escrow for keys or HSM access gating, but that will add procurement steps.

I'll draft the one-page addendum today and circulate a tracked copy. Approving this inside Novacare's procurement cycle should be faster than the full MSA.

Also: Jordan, please confirm the dev environment checklist so Chloe can confirm resource availability with Alex/Maya.

-Markus
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
